# Where to look in the Beta 1.7.3 source

<!-- Generated by tools/sourcemap.mjs. Edit the TOPICS table there, not this file. -->

The decompiled game, 675 client classes and 443 server classes.
This map exists so a question turns into a file to open rather than a search of the whole tree.

## Read the client tree

```
minecraft/net/minecraft/src/          675 classes   <- start here, always
minecraft_server/net/minecraft/src/   443 classes
```

Both trees contain the same game. The client tree is better deobfuscated — 94% of its
methods and 86% of its fields carry real names, against 86% and 71% on the server — and
the gameplay logic in them is the same code. `EntitySlime` is 142 lines in both, but the
client calls it `getSlimeSize()` where the server calls it `func_25027_m()`.

**Use the server tree only when:**

- the class is one of the 41 that exist only there (ChunkProviderServer, ConsoleCommandHandler, ConsoleLogFormatter, ConsoleLogManager, ConvertProgressUpdater, EntityPlayerMP, …), or
- you are specifically asking how a dedicated server differs from singleplayer.

## What the names look like

- **Local variables are `var1`, `var2`, …** everywhere. That is the decompiler, not a gap
  in the mapping — expect to read the surrounding code to work out what each holds.
- **`func_25027_m` and `field_401_a` are finished names**, not placeholders. Around 6% of
  client methods never got a human name. Quote them as they are.
- Getters and constants are usually named, so grep for the concept (`getCanSpawnHere`, `987234911L`) rather than for a modern name that may not exist here.

## Topic index

### A block's properties (hardness, light, material, drops)

Start in **`Block.java`**.
Then: `BlockBreakable`, `Material`, `StepSound`.

The static initialiser at the bottom of Block.java registers every block with its builder chain. Per-block behaviour lives in `Block<Name>.java`. Drops come from idDropped/quantityDropped/dropBlockAsItem.

### An item's properties, tools, mining speed, durability

Start in **`Item.java`**.
Then: `ItemTool`, `EnumToolMaterial`, `ItemFood`, `ItemArmor`.

Item ids are offset: `new Item(6)` registers id 262, because Item(int) does `shiftedIndex = 256 + var1`. getStrVsBlock is mining speed; EnumToolMaterial carries harvest level, durability and damage.

### Mob behaviour, AI, drops, health

Start in **`EntityLiving.java`**.
Then: `EntityMob`, `EntityCreature`, `EntityAnimal`, `EntityFlying`.

Start at the concrete `Entity<Name>`. onLivingUpdate is the per-tick hook, updatePlayerActionState is the AI, dropFewItems is drops, attackEntityFrom is damage, despawnEntity is despawning.

### Mob spawning: where, when, how many

Start in **`SpawnerAnimals.java`**.
Then: `SpawnListEntry`, `BiomeGenBase`, `Chunk`, `EntityLiving`.

SpawnerAnimals.performSpawning runs the pack/cap logic; each mob then vetoes with its own getCanSpawnHere. Slimes are the special case - they call Chunk.getRandomWithSeed(987234911L), which is the slime-chunk hash. BiomeGenBase holds the per-biome spawn lists.

### Terrain generation, caves, ores, trees

Start in **`ChunkProviderGenerate.java`**.
Then: `NoiseGeneratorOctaves`, `MapGenCaves`, `WorldGenMinable`, `WorldGenTrees`, `WorldGenDungeons`.

generateTerrain shapes stone, replaceBlocksForBiome puts the surface on, populate places ores, trees, lakes and dungeons. Ore vein sizes and heights are the WorldGenMinable calls inside populate.

### Biomes: which one appears where, and what it looks like

Start in **`BiomeGenBase.java`**.
Then: `WorldChunkManager`, `BiomeGenHell`, `BiomeGenSky`.

WorldChunkManager maps temperature/rainfall noise onto the biome table. BiomeGenBase's static initialiser is the table itself.

### Crafting recipes

Start in **`CraftingManager.java`**.
Then: `RecipesTools`, `RecipesWeapons`, `RecipesArmor`, `RecipesIngots`, `RecipesFood`, `RecipesDyes`, `RecipesCrafting`, `ShapedRecipes`, `ShapelessRecipes`.

Only some recipes are written out one at a time in CraftingManager; the seven Recipes* classes generate the rest in loops over a material table. Look in both before concluding a recipe does not exist.

### Smelting, fuel and furnace timings

Start in **`TileEntityFurnace.java`**.
Then: `FurnaceRecipes`, `ContainerFurnace`, `SlotFurnace`.

FurnaceRecipes lists what smelts into what. TileEntityFurnace holds the numbers: getItemBurnTime is fuel value per item, and the cook duration is the furnaceCookTime threshold in updateEntity.

### Redstone

Start in **`BlockRedstoneWire.java`**.
Then: `BlockRedstoneTorch`, `BlockRedstoneRepeater`, `BlockButton`, `BlockLever`, `BlockPressurePlate`, `BlockDispenser`, `BlockPistonBase`.

isIndirectlyPowered / isBlockIndirectlyGettingPowered on World is the read side; each component's onNeighborBlockChange and updateTick is the write side.

### Water, lava and fluid spread

Start in **`BlockFluid.java`**.
Then: `BlockFlowing`, `BlockStationary`, `Material`.

BlockFlowing.updateTick is the spread rule and the tick rate; BlockStationary is the settled form. Source blocks, flow distance and lava/water interaction are all here.

### Fire spread and burning

Start in **`BlockFire.java`**.
Then: `Block`, `Material`.

BlockFire's static initialiser sets each block's flammability (chanceToEncourageFire and abilityToCatchFire). updateTick is the spread rule.

### Crops, saplings, grass and other growth

Start in **`BlockCrops.java`**.
Then: `BlockSapling`, `BlockFarmland`, `BlockGrass`, `BlockCactus`, `BlockReed`, `BlockMushroom`.

Growth is always updateTick plus the block's own light/neighbour conditions. Random tick frequency itself is World.tickBlocksAndAmbiance.

### Light levels and the day cycle

Start in **`World.java`**.
Then: `Block`, `Chunk`.

World.getBlockLightValue reads it; calculateSkylightSubtracted turns time of day into skylight; Block.lightValue and Block.lightOpacity (both static arrays keyed by block id) are what blocks contribute. World.isDaytime and getWorldTime are the clock.

### Damage, combat and death

Start in **`Entity.java`**.
Then: `EntityLiving`, `EntityPlayer`, `ItemSword`, `EnumToolMaterial`.

attackEntityFrom is the single entry point for all damage, on both Entity and EntityLiving. Armour reduction is in EntityPlayer.damageEntity; fall damage is Entity.fall / EntityLiving.fall.

### Explosions

Start in **`Explosion.java`**.
Then: `Block`, `EntityTNTPrimed`, `EntityCreeper`.

Block resistance is divided by 5 before use, which is why data/blocks.json stores the divided figure. Explosion.doExplosionA is the ray cast, doExplosionB the block removal.

### The player: inventory, hunger, experience, movement

Start in **`EntityPlayer.java`**.
Then: `InventoryPlayer`, `ContainerPlayer`, `ItemStack`.

Beta 1.7.3 has no hunger and no experience. Health regenerates from EntityPlayer.onLivingUpdate under difficulty rules only.

### Chests, signs, dispensers and other block entities

Start in **`TileEntity.java`**.
Then: `TileEntityChest`, `TileEntityDispenser`, `TileEntitySign`, `TileEntityMobSpawner`, `TileEntityNote`, `TileEntityRecordPlayer`.

updateEntity is the per-tick hook. The paired `Block<Name>` handles placement and interaction; the TileEntity holds the state.

### The Nether

Start in **`ChunkProviderHell.java`**.
Then: `BiomeGenHell`, `BlockPortal`, `WorldProviderHell`.

The portal shape check and the 1:8 coordinate scale live in BlockPortal and WorldProviderHell respectively.

### World saving, chunk format, NBT

Start in **`Chunk.java`**.
Then: `ChunkLoader`, `McRegionChunkLoader`, `NBTTagCompound`, `RegionFile`.

Mostly of interest for explaining data values and the region file layout, not for gameplay facts.
